column1: # Expected multi-subunit system calls on the nine reference genomes
# (osmotool/test_genomes). Each row is a published or independently annotated
# expectation, taken from osmotool's README ("Multi-subunit systems") and
# test_genomes/README.md, where the original checks were run on osmo_refdb
# releases before v9. expected: present | absent | info (no pass/fail: the
# call is reported and explained in the note).
# basis: operon = characterised operon in that organism; control = negative
# control (system not expected there); specificity = the wide-window system
# must not fire outside its source organism.
# OpuB and OpuC are one system, opuB_opuC (osmotool >= 0.12.5: either label in
# each slot), because the HMMs can't tell their subunits apart; opuB_opuC rows
# expect an OpuB/OpuC-type operon, not a particular paralogue or copy number.

column5: carries both opuBA-BD and opuCA-CD; the system reports presence, not copy number
trkA and trkH both present, hundreds of genes apart
ProU (proVWX) must not be reattributed to opuA

yehWXYZ/osmF (b2128-b2131): RefSeq-annotated glycine betaine ABC transporter, a true OpuB/OpuC-type homologue. Low affinity and not osmoprotective (Lang et al. 2015), so a call here is a true family member, not an osmoprotectant system. With v11 (osmotool 0.12.5) it is absent with 2 subunits (opuBA, opuBB; no binding protein)
only H. elongata carries ectABC in this set
